output.headline: More than 165,000 back Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia
output.standfirst: More than 165,000 people, including Elon Musk, back Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia chief after his resignation over extramarital affairs, one with a suspected Chinese spy, as US treasury secretary presses for a ‘dramatic shake-up’.
output.bodyHtml:
Elon Musk and a host of other tech executives are among more than 165,000 people who have signed an open letter calling for Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's chief, days after he resigned from the multi-trillion dollar chip company.

The letter calls on the company's board members to 'bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts'.

Huang's resignation on Thursday ended a 33-year run at the helm of the AI giant he co-founded, after revelations that he had at least two extramarital affairs, one with a woman accused of spying for China and another with a subordinate.

US lawmakers from both parties are pressing Huang and Nvidia to appear before Congress and explain whether US national security was put at risk, with some in the president's own party saying Donald Trump's administration must also answer questions on what it knew about Huang's relationship with the suspected Chinese spy.

Related: 'Jensen Huang lost his mind': how AI's smartest man fell for the world's oldest trick

According to the Financial Times, Huang has discussed a possible return to the company with people close to him, with one ally telling the paper they were putting together a 'war room' of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for the former Nvidia chief's return and would try to garner support from the White House.

'Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen,' the person said, adding that the efforts had Huang's support.

Two major shareholders, the investors Brad Gerstner and Gavin Baker, urged the board on Friday to keep 'all options' open.

In Washington, however, US treasury secretary Scott Bessent said on Sunday that Nvidia should look 'outside' the company for its next chief, telling Fox News: 'They need a dramatic shake-up.'

Bessent also called on Nvidia to explain whether it had knowingly allowed its most advanced AI chips to reach China, saying this mattered more than Huang's affair with the alleged spy for Beijing.

The US forbids sales to China of the most cutting-edge AI chips, as part of its strategy to stay ahead of Beijing in the race to dominate artificial intelligence.

In late 2025, Trump authorised sales of Nvidia chips called H200s to the Chinese – but not the most advanced chips used to run AI models reshaping modern society.

'Nothing above the H200s can be sold to the Chinese,' Bessent said, adding that it was important to examine 'whether Nvidia had a culture of compliance around the US export restrictions'.

Bessent said he wanted answers within the next 10 days from Nvidia and its internal investigation into Jensen Huang's behaviour.

Alongside Musk, the tech heavyweight signatories on the letter calling for Huang's return include Tim Sweeney, founder and chief executive of video game publisher Epic Games, and Garry Tan, president of Y Combinator, San Francisco's most renowned business incubator.

Another signatory, the Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick, wrote that Huang had 'erred, yes – to err is to be human – but I do not believe anything he has done rises to the bar of separating him from his company'.

More than 7,500 signatories identified themselves as Nvidia employees, equivalent to 18 per cent of the company's workforce.

The support illustrates the unique standing of Huang, who is seen as a godfather of AI within the industry. Under his leadership, Nvidia became a pivotal Silicon Valley investor, financing datacentres and startups, earning it the nickname 'the central bank of AI'.

The company has also faced criticism, however, that it fuelled a speculative investment bubble, with Huang fighting any constraints on the AI race and clashing on these issues with Claude creator Anthropic and its chief, Dario Amodei.

Jensen Huang and other Nvidia officials have agreed to testify before Congress, officials said, though no date has yet been set.

With Agence France-Presse and Reuters
output.progress: Elon Musk is one of more than 165,000 people petitioning Nvidia’s board to reinstate Jensen Huang pending an independent investigation.

context.text: Nvidia immediately named its chief financial officer, Colette Kress, interim chief executive after Huang’s resignation, with Ian Buck and Rene Haas among possible permanent successors.
